text:
sre-oncall: alert raised — sudden uptick in 429s hitting /v1/chat/completions and /v1/generate around 03:12 UTC. dashboards show limiter pod queueing and 429 spike across multiple regions. paging @rami @sophie @leo

rami: seeing repeated `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` for accounts that should be on Dedicated tier. traffic indicates a handful of clients doing short bursts, not sustained QPS. likely scope/bucket misassignment.

sophie: deployed change `limiter-config:v2.4.1` rolled at 03:05 (deploy-bot confirmed). that release added a scoping change intended to share capacity for low-volume hosted clients; might have accidentally flipped scoping for dedicated accounts.

leo: mitigation plan — quick toggle of scoping flag to legacy, and if that fails rollback controller. doing `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/limiter CONTROLLER_SCOPE=legacy --record` now.

deploy-bot: env updated for deployment/limiter (namespace infra). CONTROLLER_SCOPE=legacy.

sre-oncall: after toggle, 429 rate reduced but still above baseline. queuing rollback as next step. `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/limiter --to-revision=21`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for deployment/limiter (namespace infra). revision: 24 -> 21.

sre-oncall: rollback finished. pods restarted and 429/queue metrics back to normal on all regions. marking as mitigation. need RCA and customer follow-ups.

rami: grabbing sample from logs for RCA. example entry:

```
2026-04-02T03:10:58Z limiter[pid=142] WARN correlation_id=bf4c... client=acct_Dedicated123 route=/v1/chat/completions status=429 limit=500 remaining=0 reset_in=60 scope=hosted
req-headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer sk-...","X-Client-IP":"203.0.113.12"}
```

rami: note the `scope=hosted` is wrong for this account (should be `dedicated`). that explains why dedicated customers hit hosted global buckets.

sophie: root-cause found in merge for PR #4620 — bad refactor in scope resolution. diff snippet:

```
- scope = determine_scope(account, tier)
+ scope = determine_scope(tier)  # bug: dropped account dimension, defaults to hosted for some flows
```

rami: tests in CI only covered host vs host sustained loads; they didn't exercise mixed-scope bursts or accounts with reserved pools. integration gap.

leo: canary + hardening plan:
- deploy patched limiter to limiter-canary (5% traffic) with synthetic bursts across mixed tiers
- add integration test that simulates interleaved bursts from dedicated+hosted keys, assert no cross-scope exhaustion
- add quick alert: fire if `X-RateLimit-Scope` header disagrees with account metadata for >1% requests over 5m
- temporarily increase burst allowance for Dedicated tier by 1.5x for 24h to avoid immediate customer impact while fix lands

support-bot: opened support ticket TKT-10021 for impacted customers. affected: acct_Dedicated123, acct_Enterprise22, acct_trial_04 and 4 additional trials. email template queued: "Transient rate limiting effected some accounts — mitigation applied, investigating root cause"

product-ops: we've got customer complaints on support channels about intermittent 429s. any guidance on credits/communication?

billing: recommend offering pro-rated credit for affected windows for enterprise customers; defer any automated refunds until we have full impact summary.

rami: preparing PR #4634 with scoped fix & tests: re-add account dimension to scope resolver and include integration test that replays a burst sequence of small completions + longer completions. pushed branch `fix/limiter-scope-account`.

leo: LGTM on the change. plan to deploy to `limiter-canary` with the following commands:

```
kubectl apply -f deploy/limiter-canary.yaml
run-tests --suite=burst-mix --target=limiter-canary --duration=15m
```

sre-oncall: adjust alerting while we validate — raise threshold to avoid noise from short lab experiments: alert on sustained >0.5% 429s for 5m instead of 1m, and add alert for `limiter_queue_length` per-pod sudden increases.

sophie: adding additional e2e scenario to CI that does: 3x quick bursts (5 reqs each) from dedicated key, then 1 long completion. assertion: `X-RateLimit-Remaining` decreases only from dedicated bucket and hosted remains unchanged.

rami: sample curl showing headers when scope mismatch occurs (for debugging):

```
$ curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-dedicated123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Scope: hosted
X-RateLimit-Reset: 165
Retry-After: 60
```

support-bot: support ticket updated — customers notified and temporary quota increases offered for the affected accounts.

product-ops: coordinate on customer notes: post status update "Partial degradation for some dedicated customers — resolved; follow-up investigation in progress." keep it factual and avoid technical jargon.

leo: follow-up assignments:
- rami: validate canary + merge #4634 (ETA: today EOD)
- sophie: add integration tests & CI job (ETA: 48h)
- sre-oncall: update runbook with scoping checks and new alerts (ETA: 24h)
- billing: prepare credit recommendations (ETA: 24h)
- product-ops: update status and customer comms (ETA: 6h)

sre-oncall: closing incident channel — mitigation complete. leaving thread open for follow-ups and postmortem drafting. tagging postmortem owners: @rami @sophie :white_check_mark:
